A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VisualOverload and provide readable main text, figures, tables, and complete appendices. Retained content can be reliably matched across the substantial formatting changes and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 37 VLMs, blind evaluations, error analyses, and appendix experiments on resolution and chain-of-thought prompting.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds image-complexity measurements, per-image accuracy distributions, and per-model error metrics.

M1.justification: The benchmark's collection and annotation procedure, question formats, answer extraction, and paired-answer scoring remain unchanged. The new Qwen3.5 complexity scoring characterizes the existing dataset without revising the VQA procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 150 artworks and 2,720 questions across six task categories, with the same stated OCR languages. The new appendix analyses reuse these images; the domain-shift discussion adds no natural-image evaluation.

E2.justification: The main comparison retains all 37 models and both chance baselines. Comparator membership in the blind, resolution, and prompting experiments is also unchanged. Qwen3.5-27B serves as the new complexity assessor, not an added VQA comparator.

E3.justification: v3 adds counting RMSE and per-model normalized OCR edit-distance reporting to Table 1. Appendix A introduces an auxiliary pairwise complexity-scoring protocol, and Appendix B aggregates accuracy by image. The original VQA splits, preprocessing, decoding policy, and resolution/prompting settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix A measures relative image complexity across all 150 images, including extremes and a score distribution. New Appendix B examines per-image accuracy for DeepSeek VL2, InternVL3 8B, and o3 to investigate domain shift. These substantially expand dataset validation beyond the retained error, resolution, prompting, and embedding analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The counting-tolerance mean-and-standard-deviation display is retained. The new parenthesized table values are error metrics, and the complexity scorer's sampling settings do not establish repeated-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v3 adds error-magnitude results for all 37 models, including o3 counting RMSE of 4.0 and OCR edit distance of 0.24, plus complexity win rates and three per-image accuracy distributions. All matched accuracy entries in the main, blind, and CoT tables are unchanged; the expansion supplies additional findings rather than performance gains.

T1.justification: Appendix A newly defines an image's complexity score as its empirical win rate across pairwise comparisons. This is a limited new quantitative definition; no theorem, proof, or formal performance guarantee is added.

C1.justification: The benchmark contributions and headline accuracy claims remain unchanged. However, the introduction broadens the bottleneck hypothesis from fixed-token encoder compression to visual representations and multimodal alignment, while the new concluding limitations qualify generalization to natural-image benchmarks.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive discussion of artistic abstraction, texture-versus-shape bias, and limits on transfer to natural images. Appendix B also newly attributes difficulty to image/question content rather than domain shift. Its claim that Figure 9 proves this attribution exceeds what the uncontrolled per-image distributions establish.

D1.justification: New Appendix I/Table 4 supplies creators, titles, dates, and source links for all 150 artworks. Appendix A documents the complexity assessor, prompt, and sampling parameters; Appendix H adds complexity_win_rate database information and the PyArrow distribution format. These substantially expand provenance and reproducibility documentation.

R1.justification: v3 adds explicit distinctions from prior art-VQA work, including VISCOUNTH and Garcia et al., extends the discussion to DocVQA and SlideVQA, and cites literature on complexity and perceptual biases. These broaden the supporting context while retaining the central positioning around knowledge-free perception in dense scenes.

P1.justification: The main six-section narrative and most prose remain intact. v3 locally rewrites the motivation and benchmark comparisons, shortens datasheet questions, and replaces the numbered appendix subsections with named supplementary sections and an overview.

P2.justification: v3 replaces the single-column format with a two-column layout, adds an artwork collage and new diagnostic figures, expands the main table, and adds the artwork catalogue. It also separates the counting panels, redraws existing plots, and relocates the unchanged blind-results table to the supplement.

improvement.justification: v3 improves auditability through complete artwork provenance, documented complexity scoring, and per-model error magnitudes, while explicitly acknowledging the art-domain limitation absent from v1. The gains are tempered by the unvalidated complexity assessor and Figure 9's unsupported claim to rule out domain shift. Overall, the documentation and diagnostic additions provide a clear but limited improvement.
